primary_topics: Remarks at the investiture of Dr. Michael M. Alba as the 11th President of the Far Eastern University (FEU), January 28, 2014

CJP's FEU origin story and gratitude: missed UP due to bus fare; FEU gave him scholarship 'no questions asked'; met Salonga, Roces, Fr. Nolan and President Evangelista -- the four people who shaped his legal, professional and spiritual life
CJP's institutional tribute to FEU: one of only five Philippine schools to produce a Chief Justice; gave CJP student leadership opportunities (FEU CSO president; NUSP co-founder)

Endorsement of Dr. Michael M. Alba: 'the right man for the right job at the right time for the right institution' -- his Stanford PhD, economics background, DLSU dean experience, and international consulting record make him ideal for FEU's 21st-century mission
sub_topics: Self-modification: 'I became... the 21st Chief Justice of the Philippines because I am an FEU graduate!' -- a playful restatement with grains of truth; only five local schools produced CJs: UP, UST, Manila Law College, Ateneo de Manila and FEU
UP scholarship barrier: same 15-centavo bus fare story; enrolled at nearby FEU 'which also granted me a scholarship'

Four FEU shapers: (1) Arts and Sciences Dean Alejandro R. Roces (at 37, later became the youngest secretary of education); (2) Law Dean Jovito R. Salonga ('taught me what I call the FEU model of legal education... combination of Dr. Salonga's insights from UP, Harvard, and Yale'); (3) Fr. Michael Nolan (FEU Chaplain; taught Catholic faith; CJP helped build the FEU Chapel); (4) President Teodoro Evangelista (served 19 years 1952-1971; overlapped with CJP's 6-year stay 1956-1960; encouraged student leadership activities)
Student leadership: first sophomore student elected President of FEU Central Student Organization; co-founded and headed NUSP (largest national student organization then and now)

FEU presidents after Evangelista: Dr. Nicanor M. Reyes Jr. (1971-1982), Dr. Josephine C. Reyes (1985-1989), Dr. Felixberto C. Sta. Maria (1989-1995), Dr. Edilberto C. De Jesus (1995-2002), Dr. Lydia B. Echauz (2002-2012) -- all personally known to CJP

Dr. Michael M. Alba: introduced to CJP only last month by FEU Board Chair Aurelio Montinola III; one hour conversation; impressed CJP as 'perceptive, knowledgeable, purpose-driven, humble and possessed of distinct educational ideas designed for the 21st century; his ideas blended the legacies of the past with the exigencies of the present and the hopes of the future'
Alba's credentials: PhD from Stanford; economics professor at DLSU and UP; past president of the Philippine Economic Society; past DLSU dean; former World Bank, ADB and USAid consultant
Closing formula: 'I believe Dr. Alba is the right man for the right job at the right time for the right institution'

notable_anecdotes: The self-modification: 'Many people know me as the first FEU law graduate to reach the highest court of the land, and later to be Chief Justice of our country. Permit me, however, to modify that a little bit, as follows: I became a justice of our Supreme Court, and later, the 21st Chief Justice of the Philippines because I am an FEU graduate!' -- the shift from 'first FEU graduate to' to 'because I am an FEU graduate' is CJP's most direct institutional gratitude statement.
The FEU Chapel: Fr. Michael Nolan 'taught me the rudiments of my Catholic faith. In turn, I helped Fr. Nolan in building the FEU Chapel' -- a rarely mentioned contribution.

Teodoro Evangelista's notice: 'Though I was only one of the 36,000 students at that time, he would see me often because of my student leadership activities, which he encouraged' -- the president of a 36,000-student university noticing and encouraging a student is the institutional recognition CJP names as the fourth life-shaping gift.

one_paragraph_summary: Delivered January 28, 2014 at the investiture of Dr. Michael M. Alba as the 11th President of the Far Eastern University, this address by CJP opens by modifying the standard introduction -- 'I became the 21st Chief Justice of the Philippines because I am an FEU graduate!' -- and notes that only five Philippine schools have produced Chief Justices: UP, UST, Manila Law College, Ateneo de Manila and FEU. He recalls his FEU origin: missed UP due to the 15-centavo bus fare barrier; enrolled at FEU which 'granted me a scholarship, no questions asked.' Four life-shapers met at FEU: (1) Arts and Sciences Dean Alejandro R. Roces (at 37, later the youngest Secretary of Education); (2) Law Dean Jovito R. Salonga, who 'taught me what I call the FEU model of legal education' -- a synthesis of his own UP (basic law), Harvard (master's) and Yale (doctoral) insights; (3) Fr. Michael Nolan (FEU Chaplain; taught CJP the rudiments of Catholic faith; CJP helped build the FEU Chapel in return); and (4) President Teodoro Evangelista (19 years, 1952-1971; noticed and encouraged CJP despite being one of 36,000 students). FEU gave CJP student leadership opportunities: first sophomore president of the FEU Central Student Organization; co-founder and head of NUSP (still the largest national student organization). He personally knows all six FEU presidents after Evangelista (Reyes Jr., J.C. Reyes, Sta. Maria, De Jesus, Echauz) but only met Dr. Alba last month when introduced by FEU Board Chair Aurelio Montinola III. In one hour, Alba impressed him as 'perceptive, knowledgeable, purpose-driven, humble and possessed of distinct educational ideas designed for the 21st century; his ideas blended the legacies of the past with the exigencies of the present and the hopes of the future.' With Stanford PhD, DLSU/UP economics professorship, Philippine Economic Society presidency, and World Bank/ADB/USAid consulting experience, 'Dr. Alba is the right man for the right job at the right time for the right institution.'
